ROW.COLUMN: (ML/CU) Patterns of Funds Transfers Between Internal Accounts and Customers

An institution`s customers may have multiple accounts that span various business lines and are not linked clearly in the institution`s transaction or account systems. This can present vulnerabilities to money laundering because the customer can, without detection, wire funds between seemingly unrelated accounts (which may be titled differently) to aid in the layering and integration of illicit funds. Understanding patterns in the client`s accounts and customers` activity with each other helps improve the institution`s knowledge of its customers and identify potential areas of concern. This scenario identifies patterns of potentially suspicious activity among internal accounts and customers, such as high levels of activity or activity that indicates the existence of exclusive relationships between accounts and customers.

The scenario monitors implicit relationships between a pair of customers. Data are aggregated at the dataset level from wire transactions records between the pair of: Originator - Benefeciary, Originator - Secondary Benefeciary, Secondary Originator - Benefeciary , Secondary Originator - Secondary Benefeciary.
The dataset also calculated the Total outgoing/receiving activity from/into the originating/ receiving customers.
Scenarios conditions are checked at the dataset level too. The match is raised in the case of high level of mutual activity.
Highlights and scoring bindings are calculated in the primary rule. The sub-rule is used for restriction the transaction records in the alert analysis.
